{{short description|German physicist}}
'''Christian Spielmann''' (born 1963, [[Innsbruck]], [[Austria]]) is an Austrian  [[physicist]] and a [[professor]] at the [[University of Jena]].

==Education and career==
Spielmann obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in 1989 at the [[Vienna University of Technology]] where he also [[Habilitation|habilitated]] in 1999.<ref name=femto>{{cite web|url=http://www.femtolasers.com/Christian-SPIELMANN.80.0.html|title=Christian SPIELMANN|publisher=Femtolasers|accessdate=January 3, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140926065646/http://www.femtolasers.com/Christian-SPIELMANN.80.0.html|archive-date=September 26, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2002 he became professor of [[experimental physics]] at the [[University of Würzburg]], before moving to Jena in 2008.<ref name=femto /> In 1998, Spielman received the Fritz-Kohlrausch-Physik Award (for achievements in experimental physics by junior scientists) from the [[Austrian Physical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|author=Karl Riedling |url=https://www.oepg.at/index.php?page=awards&subpage=winner&lang=en|title=OePG - Awardees|publisher=[[Austrian Physical Society]]|accessdate=January 3, 2014}}</ref> and in 2011 the Thuringian Research Award for his work in [[X-ray spectroscopy]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.eurekalert.org/multimedia/pub/30880.php?from=181926|title=Dr. Christian Spielmann, Friedrich-Schiller-Universitaet Jena|publisher=EurekAlert!|accessdate=December 9, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Spielmann Receives Research Award|url=http://www.photonics.com/Article.aspx?AID=46548|publisher=Photonics.com|date=April 5, 2011}}</ref>
